title: Balls or Gapes IV: Character Builder

group.text: Halfway through the evening's song, the floor shudders. The Leaking Tankard is not a building. It is an ancient Tavern Mimic, and it has just swallowed the cellar, the beer, and the urn holding the ashes of the landlady's late husband, Harold. Mags Thimbleby bars the door with a broom and turns to the room. The only way to reach Harold is down: the mimic's stomach, which locals call the Gullet, opens behind the bar. She nails up a notice: 'ADVENTURERS WANTED.' Then she looks at each of you in turn. You are strangers, all of you barefoot, all of you out of options. By the time she hands out name tags for 'Thimbleby Tankard Recovery,' you are a team.

solo.text: Halfway through the evening's song, the floor shudders. The Leaking Tankard is an ancient Tavern Mimic, and it has just swallowed the cellar, the beer, and Harold, the landlady's late husband, resting in a very nice urn. Mags Thimbleby bars the door with a broom and looks around. The only others left are Splurt, a goblin bar-back who holds his mop like a sword, and two hirelings asleep under a table: Dunk, a gentle half-ogre who carries things, and Mirabel, who holds the lantern and charges by the hour. Mags asks the four of you to bring Harold home. Behind the bar, the door to the Gullet breathes open. You are the only one who steps toward it first.

respawn_lines: You wake by the fire, whole again. Death doesn't keep people long in this tavern.
Light, warmth, the smell of stew. You're back, and Mags pours you a drink without a word.
You open your eyes upstairs in the Tankard, alive. The others are glad to see you.
Death let you go. Splurt has already set out your boots, or he would have, if you had boots.
You come back with a gasp at the bar. Mags marks it on your tab, gently.
The afterlife sends you back. It seems you still have work to do here.
You wake up alive, sore, and a little wiser. Carry on.
The fire crackles, and you are breathing again. The tavern seems to have decided it isn't finished with you.
You wake on a bench by the hearth. Dunk has covered you with his coat.
Somewhere a bard is already writing the song about how you fell. You're back to hear it.

derp.label: derp
derp.resolve: random option of the current scenario/turn, shown with a random derp_prefix before its outcome text
derp_prefixes: Derp. Your body chooses for you:
You say 'derp' with total confidence. Somehow, this happens:
Your brain goes on lunch break. Your legs improvise:
You derp. The universe, embarrassed, picks something:
A single drool of determination, and then:
You point at nothing and shout 'DERP!' Fate shrugs:
You trip over the option menu and land on this one:

rules.note: Raw d20, no bonuses. 6+ = 75% win / 25% lose (Wes, Oct 23: winning should favor the players).
rules.class_rule: each option counts for both of its classes; most-counted class wins; tie -> player chooses among tied
rules.stat_weights_status: PROVISIONAL inputs; Teacher owns the derivation math
rules.fail_forward: Fail never blocks; both outcomes advance to next scenario

scenarios.title: The Goose Incident
scenarios.text: You are three years old, barefoot in the muddy yard behind your grandmother's house in Alabamantia. A goose the size of a wheelbarrow has her pinned against the woodpile, and she is calling your name.

options.text: Grab Grandma's broom, plant your bare feet, and charge the goose.
options.success_text: The goose gives ground, then gives up. Grandma tells the story at every supper for years.
options.fail_text: The goose wins the first round and you land in the mud, but you keep it busy long enough for Grandma to reach the porch.

options.text: Step in front of Grandma and call out to the god she prays to every night.
options.success_text: Your small voice carries. The goose stops, considers you, and walks away as if it had somewhere better to be.
options.fail_text: No god answers, but Grandma does: she scoops you up, and you both retreat with your dignity mostly intact.

options.text: Let the strange heat in your chest come out, and whisper to whatever is listening.
options.success_text: The air snaps, a puff of smoke drifts off the goose's tail feathers, and it flees. Nobody ever explains it to you.
options.fail_text: Something answers, but only to say hello. The goose, unimpressed, keeps hissing.

options.text: Work out where the goose can't reach, then build a decoy from a bucket and a mop.
options.success_text: The goose falls hopelessly in love with the bucket. Grandma walks free.
options.fail_text: Your plan is sound; the mop is not. It falls apart, and the goose takes it personally.

options.text: Hum low and gentle to the goose, the way you'd soothe a frightened animal.
options.success_text: The goose settles, honks once, and lets you lead it back to the pond.
options.fail_text: The goose does not care for your song, but it is so confused that it forgets what it was angry about.

options.text: Slip along the fence and pelt the goose with pinecones from cover.
options.success_text: Three clean hits. The goose decides this yard is haunted and leaves.
options.fail_text: You hit Grandma once by accident. She still calls you her favorite.

scenarios.title: Alabamantia Barefoot Academy
scenarios.text: It's your first year at the village school. The teacher asks each child to show the class something they're good at. Everyone turns to look at you, and you realize you haven't prepared anything.

options.text: Present everything you've learned about the mushrooms growing behind the schoolhouse.
options.success_text: The teacher writes 'remarkable' on the board. Two classmates ask to see the mushrooms after school.
options.fail_text: You mix up the edible ones with the other ones and spend the afternoon at home, but the teacher keeps your notes.

options.text: Lead the class through a quiet moment of stillness before the math test.
options.success_text: The room goes calm. Everyone does a little better than expected, and nobody can say why.
options.fail_text: Half the class falls asleep. The other half is very relaxed about failing.

options.text: Track down the missing class hamster.
options.success_text: You follow tiny footprints and chewed paper to the coat closet. Hero of the second grade.
options.fail_text: You find a hamster, though perhaps not the same one. Nobody asks questions.

options.text: Show the class how strong you've gotten: lift the teacher's desk, or knock down the practice scarecrow.
options.success_text: The class cheers. Even the teacher claps, once she's back on the floor.
options.fail_text: The desk wobbles, the scarecrow survives, and you learn a lesson about overreaching.

options.text: Perform, and let the sparks that come with your nerves become part of the act.
options.success_text: The sparks dance in time with your words. It is the best show the school has ever seen.
options.fail_text: The sparks have their own ideas. There is glitter in the schoolroom for the rest of the year.

options.text: Demonstrate the little machine you built from plans in an old book you found down a well.
options.success_text: It works, and it makes toast. The book seems pleased.
options.fail_text: It butters the teacher. The book seems pleased anyway, which is more worrying.

scenarios.title: First Job at the Turnip Farm
scenarios.text: At twelve you take your first job, at old Farmer Pell's turnip fields. The morning before the harvest fair, his prize turnip, the one he's been growing all year, is gone.

options.text: Comfort the farmer and organize a search party, and swear you'll find the turnip.
options.success_text: The whole town turns out. The turnip is found by sundown, and someone brings pies.
options.fail_text: No turnip, but the town spends the evening together, and the farmer stops crying.

options.text: Sit quietly in the field and listen to it.
options.success_text: In the stillness you hear a soft scratching behind the shed. The turnip is there, half buried by a mole.
options.fail_text: You hear only wind and bees. It's peaceful, at least.

options.text: Follow the trail out of the field, wherever it leads, even into the neighbor's barn.
options.success_text: The trail ends at a raccoon guarding the prize turnip. It surrenders with dignity.
options.fail_text: The trail ends at the neighbor's dog. There is a great deal of running.

options.text: Grab a pitchfork and guard the rest of the crop through the night.
options.success_text: Nothing else goes missing, and the farmer names you Turnip Sergeant.
options.fail_text: You guard the wrong field. The carrots have never felt safer.

options.text: Study the hole it was pulled from, then rig a trap with a crate and a string.
options.success_text: The soil points to a goat. The trap confirms it. Justice arrives on four legs.
options.fail_text: The trap catches your boss. He is not amused, but he admires the knot.

options.text: Ask around the market, and listen to the whispers beneath the porch.
options.success_text: Someone slips, a shadow giggles, and the turnip turns up in a neighbor's wagon.
options.fail_text: You collect a dozen rumors and one unsettling promise. No turnip.

scenarios.title: The Barefoot Festival
scenarios.text: At sixteen you enter the Barefoot Festival, Alabamantia's proudest day, when the whole valley gathers to compete for the Golden Toe.

options.text: Enter the inventors' tent with a mechanical foot-washer and a puzzle you designed yourself.
options.success_text: The judges are delighted. Every foot in town lines up, and you win a ribbon.
options.fail_text: The foot-washer scrubs a little too hard. The judges admire the ambition.

options.text: Enter the barefoot wrestling bracket, then sprint the hot-coal walk.
options.success_text: You win both. The crowd calls you the Golden Toe, and your feet are never quite the same.
options.fail_text: A grandmother pins you in the second round. You still finish the coals, hopping.

options.text: Take on the balance-and-archery event: one leg, three arrows, total calm.
options.success_text: Three bullseyes. People bow as you walk past.
options.fail_text: An arrow clips the festival banner. It drapes gently over the mayor.

options.text: Take the stage at the talent show, as the bonfire behind you flares.
options.success_text: The crowd chants your name, and the bonfire leaps higher with every verse.
options.fail_text: The fire flares at the wrong moment. The mayor loses his eyebrows; you keep your fans.

options.text: Work the betting tables and the fortune-teller's tent.
options.success_text: You read the odds and the fortune-teller better than she reads you. You leave with a full purse.
options.fail_text: The bookie notices. You leave owing him a pig.

options.text: Judge the harvest contest fairly, while everyone offers you pie.
options.success_text: You choose honestly: a squash that grew overnight. Everyone respects the call.
options.fail_text: You accept one pie. You think about that pie for the rest of your life.

scenarios.title: The Great Possum
scenarios.text: A possum the size of a hay cart has moved into the town granary, and winter is coming. The mayor, his eyebrows still growing back, asks for volunteers.

options.text: Lure the possum out with a trail of fruit while you carry the grain away, sack by sack.
options.success_text: The possum follows the fruit out of town, and the granary is saved.
options.fail_text: The possum follows the trail into your house. It seems to like it there.

options.text: Approach the possum gently and speak to it as one creature to another.
options.success_text: The possum listens. It leaves an offering on the steps and wanders into the woods.
options.fail_text: The possum accepts your blessing and decides to stay. It's very blessed now.

options.text: Read up on possums at the library, then build something to move one.
options.success_text: Possums love to sleep. Your contraption carries the sleeping giant out to the hills.
options.fail_text: The chapter was about otters, and the contraption rolls into the river.

options.text: Charge in with a shield and a battle cry.
options.success_text: You and the possum tumble together. When the dust clears, you're on top and the town is cheering.
options.fail_text: The possum plays dead. So do you, briefly, after it lands on you.

options.text: Stand at the granary door and refuse to let it pass.
options.success_text: Nothing passes. By noon the possum gives up and naps elsewhere.
options.fail_text: It passes. Over you. Slowly. You hold no grudge.

options.text: Gather the power you don't fully understand and throw it at the possum.
options.success_text: A dark crackle, a flash of sparks, and the possum is gone. Don't ask where.
options.fail_text: The granary catches a little fire. The possum enjoys a warm meal.

scenarios.title: The Shoe Question
scenarios.text: You're ready to leave Alabamantia at last. A traveling merchant arrives with exactly one pair of shoes, and the whole town wants them.

options.text: Talk the merchant down, or quietly swap the shoebox while he's distracted.
options.success_text: You leave with the box and a friend. Inside are rocks; the merchant was cleverer than you. You laugh about it together.
options.fail_text: He raises the price, then keeps a closer eye on the box. You stay barefoot.

options.text: Study the merchant's cart, and build something better than shoes from its spare parts.
options.success_text: Wheels, straps, and a little ingenuity: you roll out of town in style.
options.fail_text: You roll straight into the duck pond. The ducks are gracious about it.

options.text: Promise the merchant something you don't technically own.
options.success_text: He agrees, and the shoes are yours. They tap-dance at midnight, but they're yours.
options.fail_text: He recognizes the kind of promise it is, and politely backs away.

options.text: Win them in the town's arm-wrestling contest.
options.success_text: Victory. The shoes turn out to be two left feet, but you earned them.
options.fail_text: The blacksmith's daughter beats you fair and square. You shake hands.

options.text: Give your chance to the poor widow next door, and pray for your own luck.
options.success_text: She weeps with gratitude. Your feet are bare, but your heart is full.
options.fail_text: She has bare feet too, and doesn't want shoes. You walk together in solidarity.

options.text: Decline. Your feet have carried you this far.
options.success_text: You walk on with calm and steady steps, your soles as tough as oak.
options.fail_text: You step on a bee immediately. Even oak has its limits.

scenarios.title: The Road Out
scenarios.text: On the road out of the valley, three bandits step out of the trees to block your way. One of them, you're fairly sure, is somebody's uncle.

options.text: Raise your stick-sword and tell them, firmly, to stand aside.
options.success_text: Two bandits flee. The uncle compliments your form and wishes you well.
options.fail_text: The uncle disarms you, then gives you some sincere tips on your grip.

options.text: Talk to them: offer to tend the uncle's bad knee, and tell a good story while you work.
options.success_text: The knee feels better and the story is better still. They escort you to the next town.
options.fail_text: The knee gets worse and the story falls flat. They let you go, mostly out of pity.

options.text: Walk straight through them, ready to tear a fence post from the ground if needed.
options.success_text: They step aside without a word. The fence post stays in the ground.
options.fail_text: They don't move, so the fence post comes up. The farmer who owns it is not pleased.

options.text: Fall back to the bushes and handle this from cover, with arrows or a smoke bomb.
options.success_text: Hats fly, smoke billows, and by the time it clears, the bandits are gone.
options.fail_text: The smoke drifts back over you, and you emerge coughing in a ditch.

options.text: Point out the legal problem with their trade, while your shadow looms behind you.
options.success_text: Between the argument and the shadow, they decide to find honest work.
options.fail_text: They have follow-up questions. Your shadow seems to take their side.

options.text: Make your hands glow, and while they stare, lighten their pockets.
options.success_text: You leave with more money than you came with, and the bandits with a story they won't believe.
options.fail_text: The uncle's pocket is full of bees. You glow, and you run.

scenarios.title: The Big City of Copperbutton
scenarios.text: You reach the walled city of Copperbutton with no money, no shoes, and a single squirrel that has followed you from the road. You need work.

options.text: Perform in the market square, and let a little magic add color.
options.success_text: Coins fall like rain, and some of them are even real.
options.fail_text: A small rainbow floods the fountain. The watch puts up a poster with your face on it.

options.text: Offer your sword to the city watch, or your back to the knights' stables.
options.success_text: Uniform, wages, and a knight who notices how hard you work.
options.fail_text: Your first arrest is your sergeant, and a horse kicks you for good measure.

options.text: Find work in the city's underside: the guild, or the sewers.
options.success_text: You are very good at this. Within a week you're paid and known.
options.fail_text: Your first job turns out to be in the guild leader's own house. You leave quickly.

options.text: Apply to the Arcane College, and open a repair stall to pay for it.
options.success_text: Accepted, and business is booming. Busy, but happy.
options.fail_text: Rejected, so you audit classes from the window while the stall smokes.

options.text: Find quiet: the park, the pigeons, the monastery steps.
options.success_text: The pigeons tell you everything that happens in the city, and the monks invite you in.
options.fail_text: The pigeons lie, and you sweep a bakery's steps by mistake. They pay you in bread.

options.text: Find honest hard work: hauling crates at the docks, or soup at the temple kitchen.
options.success_text: The dockmaster and the priests both start asking for you by name.
options.fail_text: You lift a crate with a sleeping sailor inside, then burn the soup. They bless you anyway.

scenarios.title: The Disaster
scenarios.text: Your new life in Copperbutton is going well. Then, all at once, it isn't, and by nightfall you're leaving the city with only what you can carry.

options.text: Take one more risky job, and hope the fine print doesn't catch up with you.
options.success_text: You slip away with the prize and find a loophole in the contract, just in time.
options.fail_text: The job goes wrong and clause eleven comes due. You owe someone a tavern visit.

options.text: Do the right thing in public, even if it costs you.
options.success_text: You heal a wounded stranger and expose a corrupt official. You lose your job, but keep your name.
options.fail_text: The official is your boss, and the stranger was a wanted man. You leave town quickly.

options.text: Push your work further than anyone has before.
options.success_text: The explosion is spectacular, and somehow you're hired to explain it.
options.fail_text: The explosion is spectacular, and you are asked to leave the city.

options.text: Perform at a grand ceremony, where your nerves get the better of you.
options.success_text: Sparks burst into fireworks at the perfect moment. Everyone believes it was planned.
options.fail_text: You forget the ending, and the sparks start a small fire. Applause is not forthcoming.

options.text: Step into trouble on someone else's behalf: an ogre wedding brawl, a noble in danger.
options.success_text: You win the brawl and rescue the noble. The city is grateful, briefly.
options.fail_text: The noble didn't need rescuing, and the ogres remember your face.

options.text: Let nature, and your own laughter, run their course.
options.success_text: The pigeons run the city council for a day, honestly well. You leave with a clear conscience.
options.fail_text: You laugh during the monastery's silence week. It was a big laugh. You are asked to go.

scenarios.title: The Leaking Tankard
scenarios.text: Broke, barefoot, and tired, you reach the Leaking Tankard, the last tavern before the edge of the map. Every stool holds someone who looks the way you feel.

options.text: Offer a blessing over the kitchen and buy a round you can't quite afford.
options.success_text: The stew stops moving, the room raises a glass to you, and Mags starts you a tab.
options.fail_text: The stew blesses you back, and Mags starts you a very large tab.

options.text: Take a seat by the wall, watching the doors and listening to the rats.
options.success_text: The rats are nervous, and so is the floor. Something about this place is wrong.
options.fail_text: You doze off by the fire. The rats make a note of it.

options.text: Find a quiet perch: the darkest corner, or a ceiling beam.
options.success_text: From up there you can see every purse and every exit, and the bar itself seems to breathe.
options.fail_text: Someone's already there: the tavern's cat, who refuses to share.

options.text: Claim a stool at the bar and order the strongest thing they have.
options.success_text: You drink it and see sounds for a while. The regulars nod with respect.
options.fail_text: The stool gives way. You sit on the floor with great dignity.

options.text: Light the cold fireplace with a snap, and keep an eye on the stranger you owe a drink.
options.success_text: The fire catches warm and gold, and your old debt turns out to be good company.
options.fail_text: The fire burns purple and hums. The stranger orders everything on your tab.

options.text: Fix the leaking sign over the bar, then climb on a table and start a song.
options.success_text: The sign stops dripping and the whole tavern joins the chorus.
options.fail_text: The sign leaks harder, onto you, but the song carries on.

outro_hook.text: Mid-chorus, the floor burps. The Leaking Tankard is not a building: it is an ancient Tavern Mimic, and it has just swallowed the cellar, the beer, and the landlady's late husband's urn. Landlady Mags Thimbleby slams the door, bars it with a broom, and announces that everyone currently in her tavern is now jointly responsible for the bill, the beer, and the urn. The only way out is down: the mimic's stomach, locally known as the Gullet, opens behind the bar. A notice is already nailed up: 'ADVENTURERS WANTED. Must be present. You are present.' You look at the other shoeless idiots in the room. They look at you. To make it legal, she hands out name tags: you are now staff of 'Thimbleby Tankard Recovery, LLC,' each with a job title she makes up on the spot (Chief Beverage Officer, Head of Urn, Senior Floor Apologist...). Team-up achieved.
